title: No, AI agents did not discover a previously unknown Maya site
slides: Did AI agents really find a lost Maya city?
Researchers fed LiDAR data to detection models
The 'discovery' was already documented decades ago
Check claims against peer-reviewed archaeology records
Ask who benefits when AI gets credit for human finds
thread_text:
1. AI's Maya 'Discovery' Lie

A viral claim said AI found a lost Maya city. But the location was documented in archaeology records decades ago.

2. How the AI 'Found' It

Researchers fed LiDAR data into detection models. The models flagged structures, but the sites were already known to archaeologists.

3. The Decade-Old Map

Archaeologists had mapped the area long before AI. The 'discovery' was actually a rediscovery of existing data.

4. AI Isn't the Archaeologist

AI can process LiDAR faster, but it can't interpret context. Peer-reviewed records show human experts did the real work.

5. Who Gets the Credit?

Ask who benefits when AI gets credit for human finds. Next time you see an AI 'discovery' headline, check the archaeology records first.

instagram.caption:
That "AI discovers lost Maya city" headline? The site was mapped decades ago. 🗺️

Researchers fed LiDAR data into detection models, and the models flagged structures. But archaeologists had already documented those same sites long before.

The "discovery" was a rediscovery of existing data. AI processed the scans faster — it didn't interpret them. 🔍

If you write or share content, check AI "discovery" claims against peer-reviewed records before amplifying them.

Next time a headline credits AI with a find, who do you think actually did the work? 🤔
